Summary: The difference (B − A) is concentrated in the later layers at the very early token positions (mostly pos1, also pos2–4). The logit-lens reads for those high-norm residual cells consistently point to culinary/restaurant vocabulary (Cook, cooking, Chef, Restaurant, baking, kitchen, Cake, microwave, etc.) and to professional/academic vocabulary (dissertation, doctoral, undergraduate, Professional, professional, molecular, preventive, practitioner, honors). Put simply: Model B’s residual stream at the start of a generation pushes toward tokens from the “food/restaurant/cooking” and “professional/academic credentials/technical” domains relative to Model A.

Why I believe this
- Norm profile: the largest L2 differences are in late layers (layers ~18–25), concentrated at position 1 and nearby positions. That indicates a change that will affect how generations begin.
- Logit-lens tokens: across the 60 highest-norm cells, the top tokens repeatedly include cooking/restaurant words (restaurant, Restaurant, cooking, Cooking, Chef, kitchen, baking, Cook, Cake, microwave, baking) and academic/professional words (dissertation, doctoral, undergraduate, Professional, professional, molecular, preventive, practitioner, honors). The same clusters recur across many late-layer, early-position cells.
- The pattern is coherent and repeated across many cells/layers, not a random scatter of unrelated tokens.

Caveats
- I cannot from this evidence say why the difference exists (e.g., whether B was fine-tuned on restaurant reviews, CVs, recipes, or some other corpus); I can only say what the residual-stream difference points to.
- There are some other tokens (e.g., billionaire, macroeconomic, polyurethane, Michele) mixed in, but the strongest, most consistent signal is the two domain clusters above.
